title: Number of People That Can Be Seen in a Grid
summary: Given an m x n grid of positive integers representing heights, determine the number of people each person can see.
statement: Given an m x n grid of positive integers representing heights, determine the number of people each person can see. A person at (i, j) can see another at (row2, col2) if the latter is to the right or below, and everyone in between is shorter. Return a grid where each cell contains the count of visible people.
constraints: All heights are distinct positive integers.
A person sees rightward and downward until and including the first person at least as tall; shorter people popped before that are also visible.
Return for every cell the total visible people in those two directions.
hints: A decreasing stack summarizes which people remain visible in one scan direction.
Scanning from the far end, each shorter popped height is visible, and the remaining stack top is the one blocking visible person.
Run that scan on each row and each column, adding the two counts.
Popped people have no taller obstruction before the current person, while only the nearest surviving taller person can be seen beyond them.
editorial: Popped people have no taller obstruction before the current person, while only the nearest surviving taller person can be seen beyond them.
